contexts.text: An omer for a head () = as much as is sufficient for every one. An omer = as much as is sufficient... because it was the tenth part of an ephah... and ten = what is full; hence a tenth part = as much as is sufficient... An omer is mentioned only in this chapter; elsewhere a homer, which was a measure containing ten ephahs, and thence = what is full. Illustrated.
They measured with an omer ()-the power of the reception of good; (for) an omer = as much as is sufficient; thus also power.
Two omers for one () = the power then... Here, an omer = as much as is sufficient, and the power for conjunction.
Fill an omer with it () = the highest degree of power... As an omer = as much as is sufficient, or as much power as a single one has, so also in it there is the highest degree of power.
An omer is the tenth part of an ephah () = the quantity of the good then.
The measures for dry things were called homer, and omer... The homer contained ten ephahs, and the ephah ten omers.
